name: Fisher z transformation of a correlation
expression: z = zeta_hat = 0.5 * ln((1 + r)/(1 - r)) = arctanh(r);  population: zeta = 0.5 * ln((1 + rho)/(1 - rho)) = arctanh(rho)
variables: r = sample Pearson correlation; rho = population correlation; zeta = Fisher-transformed population correlation (theta in the model sections); z = zeta_hat = its estimate; ln = natural logarithm.
notes: Worked: Moore r = 0.56 -> (1+r)/(1-r) = 3.54545, ln = 1.26567, z = 0.6328. Reconstructed from garbled DOCX fragments. effect_sizes.correlation('ZCOR', r, n) returns (atanh(r), 1/(n-3)) and raises for |r| >= 1 or n <= 3; the source has no such guard.

name: Variance and standard error of Fisher z
variables: n = sample size (number of paired observations); z = Fisher-transformed sample correlation.
notes: Approximation assumes X and Y are bivariate normal; the variance does not depend on r. Worked: Moore 1/130 = 0.00769, SE = 0.08771. Undefined for n <= 3.

name: Back-transformation from Fisher z to r
variables: z = value on the Fisher z scale (study estimate, pooled estimate or a CI limit); r = corresponding correlation.
notes: The source misprints this as tanh(r); it should be tanh(zeta_hat). Apply to point estimates and CI limits only, never to the SE. effect_sizes.back_transform('ZCOR', value) returns tanh(value).

name: Approximate variance and standard error of raw r
variables: rho = population correlation; r = sample correlation (plugged in for rho in the SE); n = number of paired observations.
notes: [R] reconstruction from garbled fragments. The variance depends on rho, so the chapter does not pool raw r. effect_sizes.correlation('COR', r, n) returns (r, (1 - r^2)^2/(n - 1)).

name: Large-sample z statistic for raw r
expression: Z1 = r * sqrt(n - 1)/(1 - r^2)  ~  N(0, 1) approximately
variables: r = sample correlation; n = number of paired observations; Z1 = test statistic for H0: rho = 0 on the raw r scale.
notes: [R] reconstruction. Equivalent to r/SE(r). Not used further in the chapter, which works on the Fisher z scale.

name: z test of H0: rho = 0 on the Fisher z scale
expression: Z2 = z/SE(z) = z * sqrt(n - 3)  ~  N(0, 1) under H0;  reject two-sided at level alpha if |z0| >= z_{alpha/2};  p = 2 * (1 - Phi(|z0|))
variables: z = Fisher-transformed r; n = sample size; z0 = observed value of the statistic; z_{alpha/2} = upper alpha/2 standard normal quantile (1.96 for alpha = 0.05); Phi = standard normal CDF.
notes: Worked: Moore z0 = 0.6328/0.08771 = 7.215408, p ≈ 0. distributions.z_two_sided_p only gives the p-value; the statistic itself is z/SE.

name: Single-study confidence interval for rho via Fisher z
expression: LL* = z - z_{alpha/2} * SE(z);  UL* = z + z_{alpha/2} * SE(z);  LL = tanh(LL*) = (exp(2*LL*) - 1)/(exp(2*LL*) + 1);  UL = tanh(UL*) = (exp(2*UL*) - 1)/(exp(2*UL*) + 1)
variables: z = Fisher-transformed r; SE(z) = 1/sqrt(n - 3); z_{alpha/2} = upper alpha/2 standard normal quantile; LL*, UL* = limits on the z scale; LL, UL = limits on the r scale.
notes: Worked: Moore LL* = 0.46093, UL* = 0.80474 -> LL = 0.43084, UL = 0.66668. The source labels the second limit 'LL', writes the generic UL with exp(2*LL*) and also uses 'LU' for UL. effect_sizes.study_ci returns the z-scale limits; apply effect_sizes.back_transform('ZCOR', ...) to each. The r-scale CI is asymmetric around r.

name: Fixed-effect inverse-variance weight for Fisher z
variables: n_i = sample size of study i; v_i = variance of theta_hat_i = arctanh(r_i); w_i = fixed-effect weight.
notes: Worked: Σw = 954 for the 8 studies. models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='fixed') uses w_i = 1/v_i.

name: Fixed-effect pooled estimate and standard error
expression: theta_hat_FE = Σ w_i * theta_hat_i / Σ w_i;  Var(theta_hat_FE) = 1/Σ w_i;  SE(theta_hat_FE) = sqrt(1/Σ w_i)
variables: theta_hat_i = arctanh(r_i); w_i = n_i - 3; k = number of studies (sums over i = 1..k).

name: Pooled Wald confidence interval on the z scale with tanh back-transformation
expression: LL* = theta_hat - z_{alpha/2} * SE(theta_hat);  UL* = theta_hat + z_{alpha/2} * SE(theta_hat);  rho_hat = tanh(theta_hat);  LL = tanh(LL*);  UL = tanh(UL*)
variables: theta_hat = pooled estimate on the Fisher z scale (FE, RE or IVhet); SE(theta_hat) = its standard error; z_{alpha/2} = 1.96 for a 95% CI; rho_hat, LL, UL = pooled correlation and CI limits on the r scale.
notes: Worked: FE z-scale 0.47917–0.60608 -> r 0.44558–0.54136 (printed 0.54236, a typo); RE 0.449943–0.632157 -> 0.42185–0.55954; IVhet 0.451061–0.63419 -> 0.422771–0.56093. Use ci_method='z' in models.meta_analysis to match the source, then effect_sizes.back_transform('ZCOR', ...). The SE is never back-transformed.

name: Percentage study weight
variables: w_i = study weight under the chosen model (FE: n_i - 3; RE: 1/(v_i + tau2_hat)); n_i = sample size of study i.
notes: Worked: Moore FE 130/954 = 13.6%; Baker FE 6.0% vs RE 8.3%. MetaXL's IVhet plot shows the FE % weights. Returned as weights_pct by models.meta_analysis.

name: Cochran's Q (computational form) and its chi-squared test
expression: Q = Σ w_i * theta_hat_i^2 - (Σ w_i * theta_hat_i)^2 / Σ w_i;  Q ~ chi2(k - 1) under H0;  E(Q) = k - 1;  p = P(chi2_{k-1} >= Q)
variables: w_i = fixed-effect weight n_i - 3; theta_hat_i = arctanh(r_i); k = number of studies; df = k - 1; H0: theta_1 = ... = theta_k.
notes: Worked: 295.05 - 517.663^2/954 = 14.15, df = 7; book p 'between 0.025 and 0.05' (critical value 14.067); exact p = 0.0485. The source writes 'Cochrane's Q'. p-value: distributions.chi2_sf(Q, k - 1). [note: the Q test has low power with few studies; do not choose FE vs RE from it (Cochrane Handbook v6 §10.10.2).]

name: I-squared
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; k = number of studies; df = degrees of freedom.
notes: Worked: 7.15/14.15 = 0.5054 -> 51%. The source states no truncation at 0; models.heterogeneity truncates negative values at 0. [note: I² depends on study precision; the Cochrane Handbook v6 bands (0–40, 30–60, 50–90, 75–100%) overlap and are only a rough guide, not absolute thresholds.]

name: DerSimonian–Laird scaling constant C
expression: C = Σ w_i - Σ w_i^2 / Σ w_i
variables: w_i = fixed-effect weight (n_i - 3 for Fisher z).
notes: Worked: 954 - 119564/954 = 828.6709. Returned as key 'C' by models.heterogeneity.

name: DerSimonian–Laird between-study variance
expression: tau2_hat = (Q - df)/C,  set to 0 if Q < df
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1; C = Σ w_i - Σ w_i^2/Σ w_i.
notes: Worked: (14.15 - 7)/828.6709 = 0.008633 (tau ≈ 0.0929, not printed). The source does not name the estimator as DL and does not mention truncation at 0; models.tau2_dl truncates. [note: DL is the source's and MetaXL's estimator but not the preferred default today; Cochrane Handbook v6 favours REML or Paule–Mandel (engine: models.estimate_tau2).]

name: Random-effects combined variance and weight
variables: v_i = 1/(n_i - 3) = within-study variance of the Fisher z; tau2_hat = DL between-study variance; w*_i = random-effects weight.
notes: Worked: Moore 0.0077 + 0.0086 = 0.01633, W* = 61.255. The book rounds tau2 before computing W*, so its W* values are about 0.001 below full precision. Use models.meta_analysis(model='random', tau2_method='DL').

name: Random-effects pooled estimate and standard error
expression: theta_hat_RE = Σ w*_i * theta_hat_i / Σ w*_i;  SE(theta_hat_RE) = sqrt(1/Σ w*_i);  rho_hat_RE = tanh(theta_hat_RE)
notes: Worked: 250.41/462.82 = 0.5411, SE = 0.0465, rho_RE = 0.49382. To reproduce the source call models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='random', tau2_method='DL', ci_method='z'); the engine default (REML + HKSJ) differs. MetaXL model code 'RE'.

name: IVhet pooled estimate
expression: theta_hat_IVhet = Σ w_i * theta_hat_i / Σ w_i,  w_i = 1/v_i  (= theta_hat_FE)
variables: w_i = fixed-effect weight n_i - 3; theta_hat_i = arctanh(r_i).
notes: Worked: 517.66/954 = 0.5426; rho = tanh(0.5426) = 0.495. Call through models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='ivhet'). MetaXL model code 'IVhet'. [note: IVhet is a model from the author's own group (Doi, Barendregt, Khan) and is not described in the Cochrane Handbook v6; use it as a justified sensitivity analysis rather than as the primary model.]

name: IVhet variance of the pooled estimate
expression: Var(theta_hat_IVhet) = Σ_i (w_i / Σ_j w_j)^2 * (v_i + tau2_hat);  SE = sqrt(Var)
variables: w_i = 1/v_i = fixed-effect weight; v_i = 1/(n_i - 3); tau2_hat = DerSimonian–Laird between-study variance.
notes: [R] reconstruction. Worked: Var = 0.0022 (unrounded 0.0021823), SE = 0.046716 (the book's 'sqrt(0.0022) = 0.046716' uses the unrounded variance). Table 10.6's 'W*' column is the per-study term (w_i/Σw)^2 (v_i + tau2), e.g. Moore (130/954)^2 x 0.01633 = 0.0003, not a weight (Doi et al. 2015). [note: author-group model, not consensus; see F-KHN10-018.]
